evidence_updates.update: A catalogued pre-1578 15th-century Joseon Gabinja physical witness (GK12436) directly transmits the same Nanjing C-II-N daily morning/evening numerical fingerprints at day0 and day178. This strengthens the daily Datong numerical-substrate component. Complete GK12437 review separately confirms the target day/night table must not be attributed to that Ritonggui object from title/metadata alone.

G893 now physically closes the pre-1578 Shoushi Type-II Beijing branch at 38.1592/61.8408 ke. Its direct mismatch with Sanming 59/41 strengthens the composite model: Shoushi supplies a method/table architecture, while the Sanming numerical substrate aligns with the Nanjing/Datong regional layer rather than raw Yandu values; exact integer reduction/change-day recomposition remains unresolved.

Direct no-OCR collation of the reviewed Yuan-shi/Shoushi conversion preserves incomplete quotients as 分 and the day/night result as 刻及分秒. This rules out same-step remainder discard as the direct generator of Sanming's whole-ke display in the reviewed received-recension scope, strengthening the composite model by making the downstream integer-reduction/binning layer explicit while leaving its exact historical rule unresolved.

Direct no-OCR re-collation of both Tianyige Ming and Siku Huqian witnesses fixes the older arrow schedule at 大寒後三日 -> 44/56 and 雨水後第九日 -> 48/52. These mismatch the exact 1578 Sanming literal 十三後日 / 後四日 transition fingerprint. The older integer-step/change-day family remains a structural component candidate, but verbatim Huqian-table parentage is now explicitly disproved; the missing layer is narrowed to recalibration/downstream binning/editorial recomposition.

Source-bound no-OCR Songshi v76 physical collation directly closes a historical threshold-driven discretization rule: each one-ke change has a separate arrow and 黃道升降差2度40分 triggers 增減改箭. This materially fills the generic post-conversion reduction-layer gap left by 12CX, but Huangyou 60/40 and its parameters differ from Sanming 59/41, so only the rule class—not the exact Sanming rule—is strengthened.

A controlled 1589 physical edition of Yueling Tongkao independently preserves both high-information Sanming-like change-day fingerprints: Yushui 47/53 -> post-day-4 48/52 and Dahan 43/57 -> literal 十三後 -> 44/56. Because the witness postdates Sanming by 11 years it cannot be an ancestor; the match strengthens persistence of a transmissible Tongshu/calendar table layer and raises the value of searching a pre-1578 common source, while direct Sanming->Yueling copying remains unproved.

HKU/FPSLRBO B17672971 fascicle 4 v11 directly preserves a Zhao Yuandu-attributed essay group and hundred-ke/half-Zi wording unusually close to 1578 Sanming. It also directly states a regional-calibration principle, contrasting old 60/40 with Yandu Shoushi 62/38. This strengthens the prose/locality components of the composite model but does not identify the 59/41 numeric parent; the manuscript's broad 1522-1619 dating prevents direct Shendao->Sanming direction from being closed.

NCL-06265 supplies a direct Zhengde-15/1520 print witness of Gexiang 時分百刻 and the closer 若子時則上半時在夜半前屬昨日 / 下半時在夜半後屬今日 wording, closing the pre-1578 textual-antecedent gate while leaving direct copying into Sanming unproved.

Direct p27 and p802 neighborhood collation shows the 1589 Yueling target fingerprint blocks carry the small source label 通書, with same-page small-font source labels such as 汲冢周書 providing typographic control. This materially narrows the common-source search to a Tongshu/almanac source family, but exact title/recension/date and pre-1578 status remain unresolved; distinct Tongshu numeric branches must not be collapsed.

Direct 360-dpi p24 collation of the Ming-print Leibian fine 四時加減晝夜節氣 branch fixes Dahan at 40/60 then 41/59 and Yushui at 45/55, directly excluding this 38/62 branch as the unchanged exact table behind Sanming/Yueling. This sharpens the generic 通書 search by proving that a Tongshu title can preserve a numerically different fine branch alongside the coarse branch.

A current union-catalog early-Ming (1368-1424) physical Tongshu witness, 《新刊陰陽寶鑒克擇通書前集》, was completely locator-reviewed across all 75 scanned pages of surviving volumes 1-4. No candidate seasonal day/night-ke or exact Sanming/Yueling fingerprint leaf was observed. This narrows the search but is not a whole-work negative because catalog volume 5 is missing from the digital object and other recensions remain open.

Xuxiu 1061-1062 directly recovers the missing front-volume-5 and back-collection boundary for Yinyang Baojian at reproduction scope, but structural review still exposes no candidate Sanming/Yueling fingerprint leaf. Copy/date identity against the current NLC early-Ming object remains unresolved, so the result narrows a search route without identifying the generic 通書 source or changing the composite ancestry model.

A catalog-bound Jiajing-30/1551 NLC physical edition directly preserves the fine 38/62 Tongshu branch before Sanming 1578, while its Dahan/Yushui anchors directly mismatch the exact Sanming/Yueling target. This closes chronology for a competing pre-1578 branch without identifying the target parent.

A securely dated 1554 LOC physical Tongshu independently preserves 選時寶鏡局 / 銅壺晝夜百刻圖式 with the coarse 40/60 branch (大寒41/59, 雨水45/55, 夏至60/40). Its direct mismatch with Sanming/Yueling strengthens the model that the target was recomposed/recalibrated rather than copied unchanged from the ordinary coarse Tongshu branch.

A distinct pre-1578 Tongshu title is now first-party census-bound to an NLC physical copy: 《通書類聚尅擇大全□□卷》, 1551 Zhicheng movable-type, call no. 14202, surviving juan 16-19. The current public Digital Ancient Books index returns no exact-title or exact-sbnumber record, so this batch narrows a concrete physical-copy acquisition route but contributes no table or numeric ancestry vote until the surviving pages are directly collated.

The 1551 NLC Tongshu Leiju route is strengthened to OPAC doc 001790345 / internal id 411999023866 / call 14202 / South Rare Books Reading Room.
